title: Sum with Two Threads
statement: Read n integers. Print their sum. You must split the work across two threads. Thread 1 adds the first half of the numbers. Thread 2 adds the rest. Wait for both threads to finish, then print the sum of the two partial sums. The sum can be larger than an int can hold.
inputFormat: First line: n. Second line: n integers separated by spaces.
outputFormat: One integer: the sum of all n numbers.
explanations: The numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Their sum is 15. Any way of splitting the work gives the same total.
The numbers are 10, -3, 7, 6. One thread adds 10 and -3. The other adds 7 and 6. The two partial sums add up to 20.
reference:
import sys
d = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(d[0])
print(sum(int(x) for x in d[1:1 + n]))
